papers.title: Solute selectivity and functional divergence of aquaporins in reef-building corals
papers.abstract: Reef-building corals are increasingly threatened by environmental stressors, including ocean warming, acidification, and osmotic stress caused by fluctuations in seawater salinity, highlighting the need for a better understanding of coral physiology. However, the molecular mechanisms by which corals regulate water and solute transport remain poorly understood. To investigate the role of aquaporins (Aqps) in coral physiology, we examined the evolutionary history and transport properties of the Aqp family in reef-building corals. Comparative genomic analyses across cnidarians revealed that the nine-member core hexacorallian aqp repertoire, comprising aqp4L1.1, aqp4L1.2, aqp4L1.3, aqp4L2, aqp4L3, glp1, glp2.1, glp2.2, and aqp12L1, has been highly conserved since the common ancestor of reef-building corals and sea anemones, whereas aqp8L was consistently absent across all examined hexacorallian species. Conservation of synteny and exon-intron structures further confirmed that major components of the aqp family architecture originated deep in metazoan evolution. Functional characterization of Acropora millepora Aqp4L and Glp proteins demonstrated that most transport properties were consistent with phylogenetic predictions, with the majority of Aqp4L proteins exhibiting water-selective permeability, whereas Glp proteins transported both water and small solutes such as glycerol. Unexpectedly, Aqp4L1.2, which belongs to the water-specific aquaporin lineage, transported not only water but also glycerol, urea, and boric acid, suggesting functional co-option after gene duplication and underscoring the evolutionary flexibility of the Aqp4L lineage. These findings suggest that the hexacorallian aqp family evolved through a combination of deep evolutionary conservation and lineage-specific functional innovation, providing new insight into the molecular foundations of coral physiology.

papers.title: Small GTPases RhoA and RhoC coordinately regulate cardiomyocyte size in the mouse heart
papers.abstract: Rho family GTPases regulate cardiomyocyte growth and cytoskeletal organization, yet the overlapping and individual function of the two primary isoforms RhoA and RhoC, remain largely unknown in the heart. Here, we examined cardiac structure and function at baseline and in response to mechanical and neurohumoral stress in mice with cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of Rhoa, global loss of Rhoc, or combined deficiency of both isoforms. Deletion of either Rhoa or Rhoc increased myocardial expression of the other isoform, showing reciprocal compensation. At baseline, Rhoc deficiency produced elongated, narrower cardiomyocytes, whereas additional loss of Rhoa restored cell width but length remained longer. Combined Rhoa/Rhoc deficiency also disrupted intercalated disc protein expression and organization and caused age-dependent cardiac hypertrophy with mild pulmonary congestion despite preserved systolic function. Following pressure overload, loss of either isoform increased hypertrophy and fibrosis compared with control groups, while combining Rhoa/Rhoc deficiency significantly worsened cardiac remodeling and systolic dysfunction. Neurohumoral stimulation with angiotensin II and phenylephrine similarly revealed cooperative control of hypertrophic growth in Rhoa/Rhoc double deleted cardiomyocytes versus either single deletion. These findings identify RhoA and RhoC as partially compensatory effectors of cardiomyocyte growth and ventricular remodeling with stress stimulation, although their individual contributions to hypertrophic growth, structural integrity, and cardiac function depend on both the nature and duration of cardiac stress.

papers.title: In Vivo Transcriptomics-Based Framework for Systematic Indication Expansion
papers.abstract: Capturing the systemic effects of drugs in vivo remains a fundamental challenge for drug repurposing strategies. Here, we present an in vivo transcriptomics-based drug repurposing framework that profiles multi-organ RNA-seq from drug-treated rodents to model systemic drug responses and match tissue-specific drug signatures against a compendium of disease signatures for indication expansion. We applied this framework to semaglutide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist originally developed for diabetes and subsequently expanded for several other indications. By harmonizing more than 900 human disease transcriptomic signatures via agentic AI and using Z-transformed reversal of gene expression scoring to quantify drug-disease relationships, our approach successfully recovered established semaglutide indications while deprioritizing Alzheimers disease, an indication for which semaglutide was not effective. Top predictions for common diseases were supported by real-world electronic health record data from the Mount Sinai Health System and several predictions for rare indications are proposed for further investigation. This framework provides a scalable strategy for indication expansion across diverse therapeutic agents, especially investigational compounds for which real-world evidence remains sparse.

papers.title: Unifying N- and O-glycopeptide dissociation methods with expedient electron transfer dissociation
papers.abstract: The glycoproteome is highly heterogeneous, where each glycosite can be modified by potentially hundreds of glycan compositions. This complexity necessitates methods that can provide glycosite-specific characterization in a high-throughput manner. Electron transfer dissociation (ETD) is particularly valuable for glycopeptide analysis, where it is critical for glycosite localization in O-glycopeptides and often produces higher quality spectra than higher energy collisional dissociation (HCD) for N-glycopeptides. Despite this, lower quality HCD spectra are often favored in high-throughput glycoproteomics experiments because the near instantaneous fragmentation of HCD results in faster MS/MS spectral acquisition relative to ETD. In short, overhead times for ETD reactions limit acquisition rates and sensitivity that can outweigh its advantages. Here we implement changes to ion handling, scan parallelization, and ion-ion reaction conditions to increase ETD MS/MS acquisition rates on the Orbitrap Tribrid MS platform. We explore fundamental parameters of ETD ion-ion reactions, including reaction q-values (i.e., Mathieu q-values) and ion-ion reaction time, showing that we can reduce the overhead of ion-ion reaction scan functions and improve the overall synchronization of data acquisition. These optimizations lead to faster spectral acquisition times for ETD MS/MS spectra while maintaining high spectral quality. Ultimately, these improvements allow the ETD scan functions to be nested within ion accumulation times needed per MS/MS spectrum, enabling ETD spectral acquisition to be parallelized within the duty cycle of the instrument and removing the major time cost to doing ETD-based fragmentation. We argue that this expedient implementation of ETD makes ETD-based fragmentation a universally beneficial dissociation method for both N- and O-glycopeptides.

papers.title: Archival data storage using DNA proximity graphs
papers.abstract: DNA offers a promising medium for long-term archival data storage, but the high cost of synthesizing data-specific sequences remains a major barrier to its adoption. Here we introduce SPAN (Synthesis-free Proximity-graph Archiving in Nucleic acids), a synthesis-independent storage architecture in which digital information is written as a physical pattern and encoded in the spatial relationships of randomly barcoded DNA molecules. Barcodes are deposited onto a patterned surface, and an enzymatic reaction records pairs of neighboring molecules. Sequencing these pairs produces a proximity graph from which the original information can be reconstructed. We demonstrate this principle experimentally by writing a 136-bit pattern using photolithography and correctly recovering 114 bits. Simulations further establish the physical parameters governing reconstruction accuracy. Our cost analysis shows that the demonstrated system already has lower estimated writing costs than existing DNA synthesis-based methods, and projects a further five-order-of-magnitude reduction using established optical writing technologies. Although SPAN requires more expensive readout, this trade-off makes it a promising candidate for deep archival storage, where information is written once and rarely, if ever, retrieved.

papers.title: A calcium-fingerprint atlas infers the signaling modes of complex elicitors and reveals a salt-like response to a humic biostimulant
papers.abstract: A central challenge in plant signaling is to infer, from an observed response, the mechanism that produced it, including perception and signaling components involved. Cytosolic calcium (Ca2+) is well suited to this reverse-engineering problem: it is a universal early messenger whose spatiotemporal pattern, the Ca2+ signature, is shaped by the specific channels and receptors a stimulus activates. We hypothesize that multiparametric analysis of Ca2+ signals can identify the main signaling pathways activated by complex or poorly defined elicitors such as biostimulants. Here, we establish a quantitative framework to resolve Ca2+ dynamics in roots of Arabidopsis seedlings by transforming spatiotemporal Ca2+ transients into multidimensional signatures. Using a normalization and feature extraction approach (Crestline), we define descriptors capturing the onset time, location along the root axis, duration, and propagation of Ca2+ signals tip- or shootwards, enabling robust comparison across stimuli. Integration of these descriptors reveals stimulus-specific "calcium fingerprints" that allow systematic classification of responses to biotic and abiotic cues within a structured signaling space. To test whether projecting an uncharacterized input into this space can predict its signaling mode, we analyzed a complex humic biostimulant. Its response fell within the fast-onset region of signaling space shared by DAMP and salt responses, clearly apart from MAMP responses, and was altered in moca1, a mutant impaired in salt sensing. Together, these findings establish Ca2+ dynamics as an interpretable encoding layer for environmental information and provide a scalable framework to resolve complex biological inputs.

papers.title: The root knot nematode effector MiEFF186 interacts with a splicing factor to reshape plant transcriptome
papers.abstract: The root-knot nematode Meloidogyne incognita secretes specific effectors to manipulate root cells and induce their redifferentiation into multinucleate feeding giant cells, which are essential for its development. A dedicated screen identified the M. incognita MiEFF186a effector as a regulator of alternative splicing, a crucial mechanism of transcriptional gene regulation whereby a single gene can produce multiple mature mRNA variants, in plants. EFF186 is expressed in the esophageal glands of nematode juveniles, and in planta, it localizes to the nucleus and accumulates in the nucleolus. A yeast two-hybrid approach identified the nucleolar G-patch protein GDP1/CIS2 as a MiEFF186a target in tomato and Arabidopsis. Transcriptomic analyses of Arabidopsis roots ectopically expressing MiEFF186a or impaired in GDP1/CIS2 function revealed changes in both gene expression and alternative splicing, with partially overlapping responses. Finally, alteration of GDP1/CIS2 expression by virus-induced gene silencing in Solanaceae or in Arabidopsis gdp1 mutants affects susceptibility to M. incognita. Together, these results identify GDP1/CIS2 as a host target of MiEFF186a and support a role for these proteins in the modulation of host RNA metabolism during nematode parasitism.

papers.title: Sugarcane bZIP16 regulates internode elongation by targeting gibberellic acid biosynthesis pathway
papers.abstract: Modern sugarcane cultivars are vegetatively propagated interspecific hybrids developed by extensive breeding and selection method to enhance sugar content, culm dimensions, desired plant architecture and disease resistance. Internode length greatly varies among existing sugarcane cultivars which determines culm length, biomass and sugar storage. Molecular factors responsible for this trait remains largely unknown in sugarcane. In this study, we characterized short and long internode sugarcane varieties and elucidated gene regulatory module interplaying with hormonal-network underneath the internodal growth. The genome size, pigment content and juice characteristics of short and long internode varieties differed with each other and correlated with gene expressions pattern. We established tissue and spatial transcriptome dataset, and comparative analyses demonstrated number of genes involved in cell cycle, cell expansion, transcription factors and hormone pathway including bZIP16 are differentially expressed between short and long internode varieties. Biochemical, DNA-protein interactions and molecular evidences revealed that ScbZIP16 inversely related to GA content by repressing transcripts of ent-isokaurene C2/C3-hydroxylase and GA20 Oxidase in sugarcane. The further genetic evidences confirmed role of ScbZIP16 in reducing GA biosynthesis pathway, flowering time and growth in Arabidopsis. This report of ScbZIP16 regulatory module offers a potential candidate for sugarcane improvement programs.

papers.title: Phenotypic characterization of an Arabidopsis stn7 stn8 pck2 triple mutant reveals only minor effects on chloroplast functions
papers.abstract: Reversible protein phosphorylation is a key regulator of chloroplast function. Although chloroplast kinases STN7, STN8, and plastid casein kinase 2 (pCK2) regulate photosynthetic acclimation and other chloroplast processes, their functional interplay remains poorly understood. We generated and characterized the first Arabidopsis thaliana stn7 stn8 pck2 triple knockout mutant. Biochemical analyses confirmed the loss of all three kinase activities on established substrates. Growth resembled the pck2 single mutant, whereas photosynthetic fluorescence parameters reflected the stn7 stn8 double mutant. Thus, simultaneous disruption of all three kinases primarily combined the parental phenotypes, with little evidence of additive or synergistic effects under standard growth conditions. This triple mutant enables studies of chloroplast phosphorylation networks and demonstrates the remarkable resilience of chloroplast physiology to combined kinase loss.

papers.title: Chromosome 7 gain establishes a just-right WNT signaling state during colorectal tumorigenesis
papers.abstract: Aneuploidy is a hallmark of colorectal cancer, yet the functional consequences of recurrent chromosome gains and losses remain largely unknown. Leveraging advances in human colon organoid culture and chromosome copy number engineering, we here identify the gain of chromosome 7 as an adaptive event following APC loss-of-function mutation. Trisomy 7 confers a cell-intrinsic fitness advantage to APC-mutant colon organoids, while selective removal of the additional chromosome 7 copy from patient-derived colon cancer organoids severely impairs colorectal cancer organoid growth. By comparing transcriptomes of isogenic disomy 7 and trisomy 7 organoid lines, we found that chromosome 7 gain promotes organoid fitness through attenuation of excessive WNT-driven stemness caused by bi-allelic APC mutation. The gain of chromosome 7 thus establishes a just-right WNT signaling state. This effect of chromosome 7 gain is conserved from early adenoma-like APC-mutant organoids to advanced colorectal cancer organoids carrying additional oncogenic driver mutations. Moreover, consistent with our organoid data, gain of chromosome 7 is particularly common in tumors of colorectal cancer patients whose APC genotypes confer relatively high WNT activity. Overall, this work demonstrates that chromosome-specific aneuploidy can act as an adaptive mechanism to optimize, rather than maximize, oncogenic signaling during tumor evolution.

papers.title: Oncogenic ETS factors expressed from fusion genes utilize EWSR1 to associate with the paraspeckle and regulate transcription.
papers.abstract: ETS family transcription factors are aberrantly expressed in prostate cancer and Ewing sarcoma due to chromosomal rearrangements resulting in fusion genes, most commonly TMPRSS2::ERG and EWSR1::FLI1, respectively. The products of these gene fusions regulate transcription together with the intrinsically disordered protein EWSR1. However, the role of EWSR1 as a transcriptional co-regulator is not fully understood. EWSR1 can undergo liquid-liquid phase separation. We found that ERG could integrate into EWSR1 phase separated droplets. We then tested the role of the paraspeckle, a nuclear membraneless organelle known to regulate transcription and include EWSR1. Both ERG and EWSR1::FLI1 associated with the paraspeckle scaffold long non-coding RNA NEAT1_2. Disruption of paraspeckles in prostate cancer and Ewing sarcoma cell lines resulted in disruption of oncogenic phenotypes mimicking the loss of oncogenic ETS factors. In Ewing sarcoma cells paraspeckle disruption promoted similar transcriptional profiles as loss of EWSR1::FLI1. Further, loss of EWSR1::FLI1 reduced the association of a paraspeckle component with EWSR1::FLI1 target genomic loci. In TMPRSS2::ERG positive prostate cancer cells paraspeckle disruption correlated with ERG-mediated transcriptional repression. These findings suggest that the paraspeckle is an important transcriptional regulator in cancers with ETS gene fusions and provides a potential target for further mechanistic understanding and drug development.

papers.title: Trp53 heterozygosity defines novel states impacting tumor plasticity and progression in Kras-initiated non-small cell lung cancer
papers.abstract: KRAS and TP53 are frequently mutated in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. The most common event at the TP53 locus is mutation/loss of one allele and retention of a wild-type allele, which confers better survival outcomes than complete TP53 loss. To study the contribution of TP53 heterozygosity, we generated a murine lung tumor model with a KrasG12D mutation and intact (K) or single-allele loss (KP+/-) of Trp53 and compared it with publicly available complete loss (KP) data. K and KP+/- mice lived longer than KP mice, paralleling clinical survival data. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of tumor-burdened lungs indicated that Trp53 heterozygosity expanded transcriptional plasticity that was not present in K and KP tumors. Genomic instability was also higher in KP+/- mice relative to the KP genotype. Trp53 gene dosage, thus, regulates phenotypic plasticity and evolutionary trajectories of tumor states across K, KP+/-, and KP tumors. Murine KP+/- tumor signatures and copy-number profiles were present in human NSCLC datasets. Two of these signatures correlated with better and worse patient survival outcomes, respectively. TP53 heterozygosity in KRAS-mutant lung cancers presents a distinct genomic landscape that should be taken into account in the development of novel therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Microglia-derived Small Extracellular Vesicles Promote Bone Marrow Monocyte Expansion and Recruitment in Glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains one of the deadliest human cancers and is characterized by a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Although tumor-associated microglia (TAMg) promote GBM progression, their role in regulating immune cell recruitment remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that TAMg-derived small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) mediate bone marrow-derived monocyte recruitment into the GBM TME. We find that these sEVs traffic to the bone marrow, where they selectively target monocytes and their progenitors. Mechanistically, sEV internalization activates MAPK signaling and inflammatory transcriptional programs, driving the differentiation and expansion of inflammatory monocytes. Together, our findings establish microglia-derived sEVs as a previously unrecognized mechanism of communication between the GBM TME and the peripheral immune system, thereby promoting the establishment of an immunosuppressive TME that drives GBM progression.

papers.title: Early-onset spontaneous murine mammary tumors show increased lymphocyte representation and reduced MHC antigen presentation
papers.abstract: Simple Summary Not all breast tumors behave the same way, and part of the reason may be inherited rather than caused by the tumor itself. Using mice that carry the same cancer-causing HER2/neu gene but differ in genetic background, we found that introduction of the PWK/PhJ genetic background was associated with tumors that appeared about a month earlier. These early tumors contained a larger proportion of immune cells, including T and B cells, but the T-cell population showed reduced expression of genes associated with cytotoxic activity. At the same time, the tumors had lower levels of proteins and genes that let the immune system recognize tumor cells, alongside higher levels of structural proteins that can make tissue stiffer and easier for cancer to invade. These findings suggest that genetic background shapes not only how quickly breast tumors arise but also how well the immune system can recognize them, a distinction that may matter for future immune-based treatments. Background/Objectives: Genetic background modifies cancer risk and phenotype in humans, but its influence on the tumor immune microenvironment and antigen-presentation machinery in ErbB2 (HER2/neu)-driven breast cancer is not well defined. We used a genetically diverse mouse cross to test whether the wild-derived PWK/PhJ background alters immune representation and antigen presentation in a NeuT model of HER2/neu-positive breast cancer. Methods: Previously, quantitative trait locus (QTL) mapping using Diversity Outbred mice and r/qtl2 identified candidate loci driving tumor onset and growth. The wild-derived PWK/PhJ genetic background was predicted to harbor genes that regulated early onset of HER2/neu-driven tumors. BALB NeuT and (BALBxPWK) F1 NeuT female mice were monitored twice weekly for spontaneous mammary tumor onset and growth. Tumor immune composition was profiled by single-cell RNA sequencing. Protein abundance was measured by data-independent acquisition proteomics in formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tumor tissue (n=5 per genotype). Single-nucleus multiome (RNA + ATAC), bulk RNA-seq, and H3K27ac datasets from the same strain comparison were analyzed for focused MHC II cross-layer analyses. Results: As predicted, (BALBxPWK) F1 NeuT mice developed tumors significantly earlier than the parental BALB NeuT mice (10 vs. 15 weeks of age; p < 0.0001). In the scRNA-seq dataset, F1 tumors showed greater representation of Cd3e-expressing T cells and a Cd79a-expressing B-cell population not detected in BALB NeuT tumors, and a distinct neutrophil cluster; F1 T cells also showed lower expression of the cytotoxicity-associated genes Tox, Ltk, Nkg7, and Gzmb relative to BALB NeuT tumor-infiltrating T cells. Proteomics identified 46 differentially abundant proteins (25 higher, 21 lower in F1), with coordinate down-regulation of Stat1, Tapbp, Parp9, and Dtx3l alongside MHC class I and II proteins and up-regulation of extracellular-matrix and elastic-fiber proteins. Focused cross-layer analysis showed lower whole-tumor expression of a Stat1/MHC II-associated gene set together with reduced epithelial chromatin accessibility at selected regions near Cd74 and H2-Aa. Conclusions: The PWK/PhJ genetic background is associated with earlier HER2-driven tumor onset, greater lymphocyte proportion, and reduced activity of a STAT1-associated antigen-presentation program despite similar post-onset tumor growth kinetics.

papers.title: Human Choroid Plexus Organoids Progress to Postnatal-like Maturation and Reveal a Closing Window of Developmental Plasticity
papers.abstract: The choroid plexus (ChP) produces cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and forms the blood-CSF barrier, yet the developmental programme driving its maturation in humans remains poorly understood. Using a 15-timepoint single-cell RNA sequencing atlas of human ChP organoids benchmarked against human tissue, we resolve an ordered differentiation process comprising cell cycle exit, ciliogenesis and ion transporter expression. Maturation culminates in a transcriptional state with features of human adult ChP, establishing the first in vitro ChP model to reach postnatal-like milestones. Centrosome proteomics identified previously uncharacterised, stage-specific regulators of ciliogenesis. To probe developmental plasticity, we perturbed ChP organoids with valproic acid (VPA), a clinically used antiepileptic and established teratogen. Early VPA-mediated disruption of multiciliogenesis and secretion recovered upon drug withdrawal, whereas late treatment washout resulted in persistent impairment of mature transporters. Together, these findings resolve the developmental programme by which the ChP reaches functionally mature identity and identify a stage-dependent plasticity window during its maturation.

papers.title: Brief communication - Phaeodactylum tricornutum is a bona fide calcifying diatom
papers.abstract: Phaeodactylum tricornutum is an unusual member of the clade of diatoms, eukaryotic marine brown algae that possess a distinct cell wall made of silica. Phaeodactylum is a rare exception in diatom biology in that it does not require silica throughout its whole life cycle. Here, we demonstrate that Phaeodactylum has a calcifying activity, which is highly unusual in unicellular eukaryotes.

papers.title: The role of the NLRP3 inflammasome in a CLN2 mouse model of neuroinflammation
papers.abstract: Neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses, or Batten disease, comprises a group of inherited pediatric neurodegenerative disorders, and is characterized by the lysosomal accumulation of the fluorescent storage material lipofuscin. The human classical late-infantile form of the disorder (CLN2) is caused by mutations in the CLN2/Tripeptidyl peptidase 1 (TPP1) gene. Comparable to human CLN2, a knockout of the Tpp1 gene (Tpp1 -/-) in the mouse leads to progressive vision loss, ataxia, motor atrophy, seizures, and premature death. While we previously showed using bulk RNA-seq analysis that reactive gliosis develops between 3 and 4 months in this animal model, the role of the inflammasome in CLN2 remains unexplored. The inflammasome is a multiprotein complex formed through pattern recognition receptor engagement, which culminate in the cleavage and release of interleukin-1 beta. Here we report that while some inflammasome-associated genes are upregulated as early as 1-month in the Tpp1 -/- cerebellum, it is not until 3-months-old that all gene transcripts necessary for inflammasome assembly and function are upregulated, leading to IL1{beta} release. In Tpp1 -/- slice cultures, we demonstrated that MCC950, an inhibitor of inflammasome assembly, downregulates transcriptional expression of genes associated with reactive microglia and inflammasome function. Furthermore, prophylactic administration of MCC950 in drinking water of Tpp1 -/- animals for two months is sufficient to lower the expression of these same genes in the forebrain and cerebellum, suggesting that inflammasome inhibitors are promising therapeutics for CLN2 and neurodegeneration broadly.

papers.title: The L-type voltage-gated Ca2+ channel CaV1.2 regulates fibroblast-like synoviocytes invasiveness during rheumatoid arthritis
papers.abstract: Fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS) are major drivers of synovial tissue inflammation and damage during rheumatoid arthritis (RA). A hallmark of the aggressiveness of RA-FLS is their invasiveness but the molecular mechanisms that regulate this invasiveness remain poorly understood. The KCa1.1 (BK, Slo1, MaxiK, KCNMA1) potassium channel is a major regulator of RA-FLS pathogenicity and inhibiting KCa1.1 expression or its activity with selective blockers reduces RA-FLS invasiveness and reduces disease severity and joint damage in rat models of RA. KCa1.1 blockade induces a Ca2+ influx in RA-FLS whose intracellular signaling results in increased cell adhesion to the extracellular matrix and thus a reduction in cell migration. However, the identity of the Ca2+-permeable channel responsible for the Ca2+ influx has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate the co-expression of KCa1.1 with the L-type voltage-gated CaV1.2 channels at the plasma membrane of primary human and rat FLS. Selective blocking of the CaV1.2 channel blunts the Ca2+ influx induced by KCa1.1 blockade and abrogates the effects of KCa1.1 blockade on RA-FLS invasiveness, migration, cell shape, and podoplanin expression. Whereas KCa1.1 blockers reduce disease severity in rat models of RA, treating rats with the collagen-induced arthritis model of RA with both blockers of KCa1.1 and CaV1.2 eliminates the therapeutic benefits of treatment with KCa1.1 blockers alone. Together, these data demonstrate a physical and functional coupling of KCa1.1 and CaV1.2 channels in FLS during RA and its rat model that regulate the invasive phenotype of the FLS through modulation of intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis.

papers.title: Host Plant and Light Regime Shape Limited, Whole-Body Transcriptional Rhythmicity in the Bird Cherry-Oat Aphid (Rhopalosiphum padi)
papers.abstract: Background Daily cycles in environmental conditions shape the biology of plants and their insect herbivores. Because aphids feed nearly continuously from the phloem to sustain rapid population growth, they maintain prolonged, direct contact with their hosts, which exposes them to plant-derived daily rhythms in addition to those arising from the environment. We investigated whole-body transcriptional rhythmicity in the bird cherry-oat aphid (Rhopalosiphum padi) under light-dark (LD) and constant darkness (DD) conditions while aphids fed on either wheat or an artificial diet sachet, sampling transcript expression every 4 h over a 48 h window. Results Only a small fraction of the transcriptome in R. padi displayed 24 h rhythms, and this fraction declined further as light and host cues were removed. Unexpectedly, more transcripts were rhythmic in DD than in LD on wheat. This trend was not present in diet-fed aphids and was not consistently detected across rhythmic detection tools or significance thresholds. Transcripts that were rhythmic in aphids feeding on wheat hosts had higher amplitudes compared to those feeding on diet. Peak expression (i.e., phase) for rhythmic transcripts clustered near dawn and pre-dusk (zeitgeber time, ZT0 and ZT12), except for transcripts detected as rhythmic in darkness-only on wheat, which peaked approximately 4 h later. Rhythmic transcripts detected in this study were functionally enriched for processes relevant to plant-aphid interactions, including carbohydrate metabolism and detoxification. Subsequent promoter analysis found E-box motifs in both rhythmic and non-rhythmic transcripts, and de novo promoter motif discovery on rhythmic transcripts identified recurring Mad/SMAD- and PAR-bZIP-like motifs. Conclusions Whole-body transcriptional rhythmicity in R. padi is limited in scope and appears strongly dependent on environmental and host-derived cues. The candidate transcripts and regulatory pathways identified in this study provide clear targets for tissue-specific, functionally minded follow-up studies to investigate the extent and regulatory mechanisms of endogenous physiological and behavioral rhythms in R. padi.

papers.title: Anisomycin-induced ribosome collisions follow a dose-dependent positional rule, distinct from the UV-induced collision landscape
papers.abstract: Ribosome collisions trigger stress pathways such as the ribotoxic stress response (RSR), yet how different ribosome-impairing stimuli shape where collisions form on mRNAs remains unclear. Here, we combine monosome- and disome-resolved ribosome profiling with proteomics of collided-ribosome fractions to compare anisomycin- and UV-induced ribosome impairment in mouse embryonic stem cells. Low-dose anisomycin, a widely used collision-inducing paradigm, does not generate collisions dispersed along transcripts but a post-initiation collision zone, with stalled monosomes and disomes accumulating within the first ~70 nucleotides of coding sequences across most translated mRNAs. High-dose anisomycin, commonly considered collision-poor, produces the same pattern shifted closer to the start codon and reduced in amplitude. These observations support a single dose-dependent positional rule, in which drug occupancy determines how far ribosomes progress before arrest and ongoing initiation supplies trailing ribosomes. In contrast, 30 min after UV irradiation, collisions are detectable biochemically but appear more dispersed, with few recurrent hotspots and preferential accumulation on highly translated mRNAs. Collided-ribosome fractions share enrichment of the collision sensor EDF1 across conditions, whereas recruitment of ZNF598 and initiation factors is most evident after UV. Our results refine the interpretation of anisomycin-based collision paradigms and show that collision landscapes depend on the nature of the stimulus.

papers.title: A Single-Cell Atlas of PVOD Across the Lifespan Reveals Cellular and Molecular Therapeutic Targets
papers.abstract: Rationale Pulmonary veno-occlusive disease (PVOD) is a progressive and lethal disease cured only lung transplant. While genetic mutations in EIF2AK4 have been identified in some cases, 70% of PVOD patients have no known etiology. Objectives To construct a single-cell atlas to define the cellular and molecular constituents driving pathophysiology in PVOD. Methods Lung samples were collected from four idiopathic non-EIF2AK4 mutation pediatric and adult PVOD patients and age-matched controls. Analyses of single-cell RNA sequencing, Xenium spatial transcriptomics, and immunohistochemistry were performed to identify cell state changes and differential gene expression between controls and PVOD and subsequent transcriptome comparison between our PVOD and published pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) datasets. Measurement and Main Results The single-cell atlas reveals marked changes in the PVOD endothelium compared to controls. EndMT and ectopic COL15A1+ systemic venous shunts and pulmonary vein endothelium are hallmarks of PVOD. Molecular analyses reveal activation of the integrated stress response (ISR)/ATF4, TGF{beta} signaling, MAPK signaling, and BRD4 are potential key players in the pathophysiology of PVOD. While PVOD and PAH share both pathological and some molecular mechanisms, ISR and TGF{beta} signaling are more prominent in PVOD than PAH. Conclusions These data indicate that endothelial dysfunction is a primary etiology in the development of PVOD with activation of multiple pathways with druggable targets.

papers.title: Comprehensive calculation of product and ATP yields for glucose fermentation
papers.abstract: Lignocellulose sugars are degraded anaerobically by microbial communities as part of the carbon cycle, yielding short- and medium-chain fatty acids as intermediates and carbon dioxide and methane as final products. The underlying metabolic network is branched and its product yields depend on environmental conditions. We compiled a pan-catabolic network of the anaerobic digestion of glucose into 11 fermentation products, including alcohols, acids, and ketones. It consists of 75 reactions and incorporates energy conservation via substrate-level phosphorylation and transport-coupled phosphorylation, with ferredoxin, NADH, and quinol as electron carriers. We calculated all net conversions of glucose into fermentation products and their ATP yields. We find 195,629 unique conversions (about 50% with non-zero ATP yield), including known and many novel ones. Conversions with identical product stoichiometry can differ in ATP yield: glucose to propionate and acetate is achieved by different subnetworks with 23 distinct ATP/glucose yields, and even glucose to lactate shows 12 yields ranging from 0 to 4.5. The driving force of the conversions decreases with ATP yield, whereas the number of reactions used does not correlate with it. The known catabolic conversions underlying anaerobic digestion might thus be only the tip of the iceberg.

papers.title: Engineered cells that sense and respond to interleukin-23 with neutralizing therapy for autoimmunity
papers.abstract: Engineered cell sensors are powerful tools for monitoring biomarkers and delivering timely therapy. Here we create an engineered cell sensor of interleukin-23 (IL-23), a critical biomarker in many autoimmune diseases, and a therapeutic delivery platform for autoimmune disease management. We utilized Modular Extracellular Sensor Architecture (MESA), a promising platform given its modularity and previously developed cell sensors for immune targets such as IL-10. First, we developed a library of IL-23 MESA receptors by incorporating IL-23-specific nanobody binders and performed high-throughput functional screening. We achieved further receptor optimization by modifying the extracellular linker length and the ratio of receptor chain expression. Receptor performance was highly correlated with predicted geometric features such as binder pair distance and degree of transmembrane domain dimerization. The receptors were limited by poor surface expression and functioned most effectively as sensors for intracellular IL-23. Finally, we modified the IL-23 sensing circuit to output an IL-23 neutralizing nanobody with the potential to reduce inflammation triggered by IL-23 secretion. This sense-and-respond architecture can be utilized for dynamic therapeutic treatment to meet the dynamic relapse-remitting pattern of many autoimmune diseases.

papers.title: Soil microbiome effects on quantitative floral traits of the annual plant Mimulus guttatus
papers.abstract: Plant flowering is a critical determinant of fitness and supports pollination services to ecosystems. Flowers are energetically expensive and require nutrients that plants might otherwise use for growth. Soil microorganisms can alter plant development in a variety of ways, but the quantitative importance of microbiomes in determining floral variation has yet to be established. In particular, it is unclear the extent to which genotypic differences in flowering phenotypes are mediated through the microbiome. We used a two-generation plant-soil feedback design to test whether flowering traits in a short-lived annual plant Mimulus guttatus drive differentiation in rhizosphere microbiomes. Second, we tested whether these microbiomes subsequently affected flowering traits of progeny plants. We found that different plant genotypes did not generate differences in rhizosphere microbiome structure or diversity after eight weeks of growth. When these microbiomes were inoculated onto new plants, flowering traits were mainly driven by the progeny plants genotype and not the genotype of the parental plant that trained the inoculated microbiome. Longer microbial training, as would necessarily happen in perennial plants, may produce stronger effects, but our results suggest microbiome effects contribute mainly to the environmental noise in flower traits in the short-lived annual Mimulus guttatus.

papers.title: Rye stem rust is a reservoir of diversity and virulence for wheat stem rust
papers.abstract: Sexual populations of the stem rust pathogen (Puccinia graminis or Pg) are producing new race types globally. An analysis of 385 Pg genomes (204 from this study) illuminated international migration and admixture events. Within Kazakhstan, a novel and diverse sexual clade of P. graminis is described. An analysis of the highly divergent mating type homeodomain (HD) locus found that the 75 Kazakhstan isolates had 41 different HD haplotypes, out of a total of 99 P. graminis HD haplotypes found globally. Kazakh isolates share HD haplotypes with isolates in clade 1 (Ug99), 3-B (TTRTF), and 4 (TKTTF). There are 148 unique combinations of HD locus haplotypes within the 385 isolates. Rye (Pgs) and wheat (Pgt) stem rust share multiple HD locus haplotypes and have conserved pheromone receptors and precursors, while oat stem rust (Pga) does not. Virulent alleles for AvrSr13, AvrSr22, and AvrSr50 in Pgt are frequently derived from admixture with Pgs. Pgs also contains virulent effectors for AvrSr33, AvrSr62, and AvrSr27. Pgt isolates virulent on Sr31, such as Ug99 and isolates from Spain, have genetic links to North American Pgs isolates which are present in regions of the United States where barberry is common.

papers.title: Predicting resistance to synthetic lethal therapies in cancer
papers.abstract: Background Synthetic lethality (SL) occurs when an alteration in one gene renders cells vulnerable to inhibition of another, offering a strategy for targeted cancer therapy. PARP inhibitors represent the first clinically approved synthetic lethal therapy, and numerous additional candidates are now in clinical trials. Unfortunately, resistance to these therapies is common and impairs their overall effectiveness. Although there is a growing understanding of the factors that predict synthetic lethal interactions, the prediction of mechanisms driving resistance to these effects remains largely unstudied. Here, we sought to determine whether SL resistance could be predicted a priori using protein-protein interaction networks integrated with additional molecular profiles. Methods We curated genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 chemogenetic resistance screens spanning ten unique SL biomarker-target pairs. For each pair, we extracted resistance genes and computed features capturing protein-protein interactions, gene expression, and essentiality. We compared these features between resistance and non-resistance genes and developed a random forest classifier to predict resistance. Model performance was assessed using random-split and structured leave-one-out schemes based on biomarkers, targets, and SL pairs to ensure robust generalisation. Independent validation of the model was performed by assessing its ability to predict resistance to two SL therapies currently in clinical trials, MTAP-PRMT5 and ATM-ATR. Results Resistance genes were significantly enriched among the protein-protein interaction partners of SL pairs across multiple datasets, suggesting functional interaction networks can aid the prioritisation of resistance mechanisms. Resistance genes tended to be more co-expressed with their associated target and also displayed distinct essentiality patterns. Although no individual feature was strongly predictive, integrating all features in a random forest model improved discrimination between resistance and non-resistance genes. Under leave-one-SL-pair-out cross-validation - our most stringent test of generalisation - the model achieved a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.72 across ten pairs (range 0.57-0.91; mean average precision ~9%); a random train-test split gave a higher AUROC (~0.78) that we treat as an optimistic upper bound, since biomarkers and targets are shared across folds. Average precision remained low in absolute terms, reflecting the inherent challenge of predicting extremely rare resistance events (<1% of genes). Conclusions Resistance to synthetic lethal therapies arises, at least in part, from predictable patterns of network connectivity, transcriptional coordination, and context-dependent essentiality. Our integrative framework provides a computational approach for anticipating resistance mechanisms across the expanding landscape of synthetic lethal therapies, offering a foundation for designing more durable and effective combination treatments.

papers.title: LuTuFlow: a deep learning-based pipeline for quantitative characterization of mouse lung tumors in CT imaging
papers.abstract: Computed tomography (CT) is a widely used, non-invasive imaging tool to monitor tumor growth. Tumor identification and volumetric quantification are crucial for assessing tumor burden, whereas tracking individual tumors by aligning scans from multiple time points reveals disease progression. However, these processes remain largely dependent on manual analysis, limiting the accuracy, reproducibility, objectivity, and scalability of tumor characterization. Several deep learning models have enabled automated segmentation and object identification. However, open-source, integrated software platforms that cover the entire workflow - including processing raw CT images, annotating and tracking tumors through time, and generating data reports and visualizations - are still needed. Here, we present LuTuFlow, a computer vision pipeline incorporating a nnU-Net-based deep learning model, configured for murine lung segmentation and tumor analysis. We integrated these modules into a Napari plugin, allowing researchers to apply the entire automated workflow to transform raw CT scan datasets into quantitative readouts and interactive visualizations in a simple graphical user interface. The resulting model, iteratively refined using expert-corrected annotations, generated reliable quantitative estimates of tumor burden.

papers.title: A low-androgen environment sustains redox-active sGC states required to restrain castration-resistant prostate cancer growth via elevated cGMP levels
papers.abstract: Castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) remains incurable and fatal, creating a dire need for new safe and effective treatment strategies. We recently reported that the soluble guanylyl cyclase (sGC) stimulator, riociguat, cooperates with standard-of-care androgen deprivation (AD) to inhibit castration-resistant tumor burden by oxygenating hypoxic tumor niches and inducing tumor apoptosis. We further found that AD restores the sensitivity of CRPC cells to riociguat, which requires a redox-active functional sGC complex to stimulate cyclic GMP (cGMP) production. As redox reprogramming is a feature of the low-androgen PC milieu, to better establish the parameters of riociguat efficacy, we wished to determine whether redox-inactive forms of sGC persist in the castrate setting. To do so, we treated CRPC LNAI tumor-bearing animals with cinaciguat, an sGC activator which preferentially acts on the oxidized sGC complex. We found that, compared to riociguat, cinaciguat did not significantly increase intratumoral or systemic cGMP levels in the castrate setting. Nor did cinaciguat treatment significantly decrease tumor burden or oxygenate the hypoxic CRPC tumors. Given the preferential activity of cinaciguat on the redox-inactive sGC complex, our results indicate that the low-androgen castrate setting maintains the sGC complex in its functionally reduced state, affirming the critical benefit of AD for riociguat efficacy in the lethal castration-resistant disease stage.

papers.title: Biomarker-driven and gene-enhanced viral therapy for malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor
papers.abstract: Background: High-grade malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNST) frequently lose Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2), reducing the repressive histone mark, H3K27me3. We hypothesized that H3K27me3 loss sensitizes MPNST to oncolytic HSV due to impaired transcriptional resistance. HSV replication is also restricted by the integrated stress response, normally countered by HSV ICP34.5, representing an additional resistance pathway to ICP34.5-attenuated HSV. Methods: PRC2 loss-of-function was evaluated as a biomarker of HSV G47{Delta} ({Delta}ICP34.5) susceptibility in MPNST using isogenic, pharmacologic inhibition, and genetic rescue models. CUT&RUN and RNA-sequencing defined PRC2-dependent viral and host responses. We engineered a G47{Delta}-derived vector (G47{Delta}2) with tumor-regulated ICP34.5 expression [G47{Delta}2,ins(BIRC5>ICP34.5)] and evaluated efficacy in MPNST xenografts. Results: H3K27me3 deficiency increased G47{Delta} sensitivity and viral spread in vitro. CUT&RUN demonstrated PRC2-dependent H3K27me3 accumulation on the viral genome, explaining G47{Delta} activity in H3K27me3-deficient MPNST. RNA sequencing of G47{Delta} infected MPNST cells revealed heightened integrated stress response activity and blunted induction of translation-associated programs in the PRC2-deficient state (both p<0.001), consistent with compensatory resistance at the level of viral protein translation. Accordingly, tumor-regulated ICP34.5 HSV limited daily tumor-volume growth to 0.6% (95% CI, -2.9-4.2%), improving upon both G47{Delta}2 (8.3%; 4.5-12.2%) and controls (22.5%; 17.4-27.8%). A murine gastrointestinal toxicity phenotype reduced all-cause event-free survival, indicating vector and dosing optimizations are needed to widen the therapeutic window. Conclusions: H3K27me3 loss creates a paradoxical antiviral state that tumor-selective ICP34.5 overcomes to rescue HSV anti-tumor activity, supporting biomarker-driven viral engineering to exploit the permissive transcriptional state of H3K27me3-deficient MPNSTs.

papers.title: Dysregulation of epithelial differentiation architecture underlies field cancerization in head and neck cancer
papers.abstract: Cell-by-cell and gene-by-gene relationships, such as kernels and correlations, shape most single-cell analyses but are rarely inspected directly due to a lack of visualization tools that display them. AnnZarro is a point-and-click browser viewer that shows these matrices linked to an AnnData object's cells x genes data. Using AnnZarro, experimental biologists can explore data without code and computational biologists can probe the relationships behind their analyses. One focused cell and one focused gene drive every panel. Clicking a cell paints its row of any cell-by-cell matrix over an embedding or spatial coordinates; clicking a gene paints its row of any gene-by-gene matrix over a gene plot such as a volcano. The focus also links genes to the cells where they change, and cells to the genes that distinguish them. AnnZarro reads only the matrix rows and columns each panel displays from zarr stores and hence users can explore matrices far larger than memory on a laptop or a shared server. Large datasets open on a reproducible subset, and users step through the remaining cells in parts. On a laptop, a 100,000-cell part of Tahoe-100M opens in 4 s and stays interactive. With the subset switched off, AnnZarro draws all 95.6 million cells in one plot in about 5 to 7 s. This tutorial prepares a dataset with Kompot differential abundance and expression, a diffusion kernel and gene correlations, then explores it in six worked examples. AnnZarro is available at https://annzarro.readthedocs.io.
